presentingComplaint: 6 weeks of malaise, low-grade fever and weight loss, now with blood-streaked sputum, a purpuric rash on the legs and reduced urine output.
history: Previously well retired schoolteacher with a 6-week history of drenching malaise, intermittent low-grade fevers, night sweats and 5 kg unintentional weight loss. Over the preceding 2 months he had recurrent 'sinus infections' with persistent nasal crusting, blood-tinged nasal discharge and a new-onset epistaxis, treated twice with oral antibiotics by his GP without benefit. In the last 10 days he developed migratory joint pains (wrists, knees, ankles), small-volume haemoptysis and a non-blanching rash over both shins. Family reported darker, frothy urine and ankle swelling. No recent travel, no injection drug use, no prosthetic valve, no dental work. The overlapping picture (fever, purpura, haemoptysis, renal impairment) initially prompted an infective endocarditis and pneumonia-with-glomerulonephritis workup, but blood cultures were repeatedly negative and echocardiography showed no vegetations, redirecting attention to a systemic vasculitis.
examination: Frail-looking, mildly pale. Nasal mucosa crusted with a shallow septal ulcer and early saddling of the nasal bridge. Chest: scattered bilateral crepitations, no focal consolidation. Palpable purpura over both lower legs with a few early ulcerated lesions; no splinter haemorrhages, no Osler nodes, no Janeway lesions. Cardiovascular: no murmur, no stigmata of endocarditis. Mild bilateral pitting ankle oedema. Wrists and knees mildly swollen and tender without effusion. Fundi and cranial nerves normal; foot-drop absent.

labs.urinalysis: 3+ blood, 2+ protein, dysmorphic red cells with red-cell casts (active nephritic sediment)
labs.pr3_anca: positive, strongly (c-ANCA by IF, PR3 by ELISA >180 U/mL)

imaging: CT chest: multiple bilateral nodules, two with early cavitation, and patchy ground-glass opacities in keeping with pulmonary haemorrhage; no lobar consolidation or empyema. Transthoracic (and subsequent transoesophageal) echocardiography: structurally normal valves, no vegetation. CT sinuses: mucosal thickening with bony erosion of the nasal septum.
microbiology: Three sets of blood cultures negative at 5 days. Sputum bacterial culture and AFB smear negative; sputum Xpert MTB/RIF not detected. Urine culture no growth. No microbiological source identified despite thorough sepsis screen.
differentialDiagnoses: ANCA-associated vasculitis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis) — pulmonary-renal syndrome (leading diagnosis)
Infective endocarditis with immune-complex glomerulonephritis and septic emboli (excluded: negative cultures, no vegetation)
Rapidly progressive (pauci-immune) glomerulonephritis of other cause
Systemic lupus erythematosus flare with pulmonary-renal involvement
Community-acquired / cavitating pneumonia with reactive changes
finalDiagnosis: Systemic vasculitis — PR3-ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis presenting as a pulmonary-renal syndrome, mimicking culture-negative infective endocarditis.
citations: ACR/Vasculitis Foundation — Guideline for the Management of ANCA-Associated Vasculitis, 2021
KDIGO — Clinical Practice Guideline for Glomerular Diseases (ANCA-Associated Vasculitis), 2021
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — The Vasculitis Syndromes
stewardship: Non-infective diagnosis: no empiric antibiotics indicated once endocarditis and infection are excluded. Management is immunosuppression (high-dose glucocorticoids plus rituximab or cyclophosphamide); PJP prophylaxis (co-trimoxazole) is given as part of the immunosuppression protocol, not as treatment of infection.
contraindications: Do not start empiric antibiotics for presumed sepsis/endocarditis once cultures are negative and echocardiography is clear — anchoring on infection delays immunosuppression.
Avoid nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, iodinated contrast without hydration, aminoglycosides) given active RPGN.
Screen for latent TB, hepatitis B/C and quantify infection risk before rituximab/cyclophosphamide and steroids.
edgeCases: Culture-negative endocarditis can itself produce ANCA positivity and pauci-immune GN — repeat cultures, exclude vegetations, and correlate before committing to immunosuppression.
Alveolar haemorrhage may present with normal or only mildly low SpO2 early; a falling haemoglobin with diffuse ground-glass change is the clue.
Anti-GBM disease can coexist with PR3/MPO-ANCA (double-positive) — always send anti-GBM in a pulmonary-renal syndrome.
expectedNextQuestions: Any preceding chronic sinusitis, nasal crusting, epistaxis or hearing loss (ENT involvement of GPA)?
Any numbness, tingling or foot-drop suggesting mononeuritis multiplex?
Quantify haemoptysis and check for a falling haemoglobin to gauge alveolar haemorrhage.
Drug and infection history to exclude endocarditis, drug-induced (e.g. hydralazine/PTU) ANCA vasculitis, and cocaine/levamisole exposure.
expectedInvestigations: ANCA panel (PR3/c-ANCA and MPO/p-ANCA by ELISA and IF)
Anti-GBM antibody and ANA/complement to exclude mimics
Repeated blood cultures and transoesophageal echocardiography to exclude endocarditis
Urinalysis with microscopy for dysmorphic RBCs/red-cell casts and urine protein:creatinine ratio
Renal biopsy for pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis

investigations: Urine microscopy for red-cell casts and protein:creatinine ratio
Blood cultures and echocardiography to exclude endocarditis
